events.title: Cfront 3.0 adds templates to C++
events.summary: AT&T's Cfront 3.0 release was the first C++ compiler to support templates, enabling generic programming in production code.
events.about: Templates let one C++ function or class work with many types — e.g. a generic `vector<int>` or `vector<string>` without copy-pasting code. This became the basis for the STL and modern C++ library design (sort, map, smart pointers).

narrative.whyChosen: Templates unlocked the STL era and changed how C++ libraries were designed.
narrative.whyImportant: Generic containers and algorithms became possible without sacrificing performance.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers duplicated type-specific code or used void pointers; templates provided compile-time polymorphism.
